title: This Eric Trump-Backed Startup Just Got AMD's Chips for Its Humanoid Robots— Now It's Building Military Versions Too, Reviving Conflict-Of-Interest Fears
excerpt: Eric Trump-backed Foundation Future Industries will use Advanced Micro Devices Inc. chips to develop autonomous humanoid robots for factories and military op...

Eric Trump-backed Foundation Future Industries will use Advanced Micro Devices Inc. chips to develop autonomous humanoid robots for factories and military operations, with industrial customers paying about $100,000 annually to lease each machine.

AMD Chips Power Next Phantom Robot

According to a Reuters report, Foundation Future Industries said on Thursday that AMD's Ryzen AI Embedded X100 Series processors will power the Phantom MK-2. The companies did not disclose financial terms. Eric Trump, who invested in the startup earlier this year, serves as chief strategy adviser.

AMD introduced the X100 family in January as part of a push into embedded artificial intelligence and autonomous systems. The processors combine Zen 5 CPU cores, RDNA 3.5 graphics and an XDNA 2 neural-processing unit, allowing robots to run perception, reasoning and control workloads locally. AMD says the portfolio targets "physical AI for autonomous systems, including humanoid robotics."

The deal extends AMD's reach beyond data-center accelerators and AI PCs into edge computing, where machines must process sensor data and respond in real time. AMD has positioned its embedded AI portfolio for industrial automation, vehicles and humanoid robotics.

Foundation Plans Major Humanoid Production Expansion

Foundation, founded in 2024, told Reuters that its Phantom MK-1 robots helped build more than 24,000 vehicles in 2025. CEO Sankaet Pathak said the company will open a factory in October capable of producing 5,000 Phantom robots annually.

The startup plans to begin building another facility early next year with capacity for 50,000 robots per year. Together, the plants could eventually produce 55,000 units annually, although Foundation did not identify customers or disclose confirmed orders.

Industrial customers will lease each robot for about $100,000 per year. Foundation is separately developing $300,000 defense variants for government buyers, targeting materials handling and reconnaissance.

Defense Push Revives Conflict Of Interest Concerns

The military push places Foundation within the expanding defense-autonomy market. Eric Trump and his brother Donald Trump Jr. have also backed drone and robotics companies including XTEND, Unusual Machines Inc. and Powerus. Eric Trump had earlier invested in XTEND's planned $1.5 billion U.S. listing.

埃里克·特朗普支持的未来工业基金会将使用 Advanced Micro Devices Inc. 芯片开发用于工厂和军事行动的自主人形机器人，工业客户每年支付约 10 万美元租赁每台机器。

AMD 芯片为下一代 Phantom 机器人提供动力

据路透社报道，未来工业基金会周四表示，AMD 的 Ryzen AI Embedded X100 系列处理器将为 Phantom MK-2 提供动力。 两家公司没有透露财务条款。 埃里克·特朗普今年早些时候投资了这家初创公司，担任首席战略顾问。

AMD 在 1 月份推出了 X100 系列，作为进军嵌入式人工智能和自主系统的一部分。 这些处理器结合了 Zen 5 CPU 内核、RDNA 3.5 显卡和 XDNA 2 神经处理单元，使机器人能够在本地运行感知、推理和控制工作负载。 AMD 表示，该产品组合的目标是“用于自主系统的物理人工智能，包括人形机器人”。

这笔交易将 AMD 的业务范围从数据中心加速器和人工智能 PC 扩展到边缘计算，其中机器必须处理传感器数据并实时响应。 AMD 已将其嵌入式人工智能产品组合定位于工业自动化、车辆和人形机器人。

基金会计划扩大人形生物生产规模

成立于 2024 年的 Foundation 告诉路透社，其 Phantom MK-1 机器人在 2025 年帮助制造了超过 24,000 辆汽车。 首席执行官 Sankaet Pathak 表示，该公司将于 10 月开设一家工厂，每年可生产 5,000 台 Phantom 机器人。

该初创公司计划明年初开始建造另一座工厂，每年可容纳 50,000 台机器人。 尽管基金会没有透露客户身份或透露已确认的订单，但这些工厂最终每年可生产 55,000 件。

趋势：避免第一大投资错误：你的“安全”持仓可能会让你付出巨大的代价

工业客户将以每年约 10 万美元的价格租赁每个机器人。 基金会正在为政府买家单独开发价值 300,000 美元的防御变体，目标是材料处理和侦察。

国防推动重燃利益冲突担忧

军事推动使基金会进入了不断扩大的国防自主市场。 埃里克·特朗普和他的兄弟小唐纳德·特朗普还支持了无人机和机器人公司，包括 XTEND、Unusual Machines Inc. 和 Powerus。 埃里克·特朗普 (Eric Trump) 早些时候投资了 XTEND 计划在美国上市的 15 亿美元资金。
